forecasts.reason: Removing 12 steps at about 16 ms each saves about 0.18 s. The dose curve should bend: the second trim costs about 0.1–0.15 pp from a population mean near 0.752, so seeds 0–2 clearing 0.753 is under a coin flip.

Group 3 runs on small maps (7×7, then 3×3), where kernels are less efficient, so cutting about 18% of its MACs saves only about 2–3% of time (~0.12 s). On a capacity-limited 100-way head it loses ~0.2–0.3 pp, which is a rate near or worse than the dial's 0.77 s/pp.

This saves about 2–2.5 ms per unfrozen step plus BN/GELU traffic, about 0.2 s in total (≈4%, below the 5% the hypothesis needs). Depth cuts in the learning stem cost steps-worth of accuracy (~0.3 pp).
24 px steps run at 20 px save about 5 ms × 24 ≈ 0.12 s (~2.4%). E033/E026 suggest early resolution is nearly free, but the 20→28 jump may cost ~0.1 pp, and 3 seeds cannot resolve that.
The change costs no time. On a short under-fitting run, LS 0.3 vs 0.15 is probably within ±0.1 pp; E013 showed no detectable effect.

cruxes: Is the early 20 px trim dose curve linear or convex? Does a second −12 steps cost ≤0.1 pp (as E061 did) or ≥0.2 pp, which is the dial rate?
Is the tip's unselected population mean ≈0.7525 or ≈0.7535? This decides whether any −0.1 pp change can still clear 0.753 on seeds 0–2.
Do small-map layers (group 3 at 7×7/3×3, group-1 conv2/3 at 15×15) scale time with MACs, or are they launch- and bandwidth-bound so that width and depth cuts save under half their FLOP share?
structured_output.world_model: The tip is E061 (225 steps, 5.02 s, 0.7534 on seeds 0–2), with a population mean of about 0.752–0.7525. Time ≈ 0.25 s + Σ steps × per-step cost: 32 px 32 ms, 28 px 26 ms, 24 px 21 ms, 20 px 16 ms. A stem-frozen step saves 8.7 ms, and freezing group 2 as well saves about 10 ms more. The epoch dial trades about 0.77–0.8 s per pp. Accuracy is bought with optimizer steps on layers that are still learning; truncation is free only after a layer finishes. The remaining levers are early 20 px trims and resolution swaps (~0.12–0.18 s each, at near-dial cost) and width or depth cuts, which save less than their MAC share on small maps. Label smoothing is likely flat. Every candidate sits under a coin flip for clearing the 0.753 local bar.
